fig1_euler_vs_rk4.svg: The harmonic oscillator $y''=-y$ in the phase plane $(y,y')$, both schemes taking the same coarse step $\Delta t\approx0.1$ via integrate. The exact motion is the unit circle (constant energy); explicit Euler (orange) gains energy and spirals outward, while RK4 (blue) — fourth order — stays on the orbit. This is why RK4 is the workhorse integrator.
fig2_linear_saddle.svg: Flow of $\dot{\mathbf{x}}=A\mathbf{x}$ for $A=[[0,1],[1,0]]$. Diagonalizing with the MA-04 eigensolver gives eigenvalues $\lambda=\pm1$; the exact solution $\mathbf{x}(t)=\sum_i(\mathbf{v}_i\!\cdot\!\mathbf{x}_0)e^{\lambda_i t}\mathbf{v}_i$ (purple streamlines, from linear_evolve_symmetric) is a saddle that grows along the $\lambda=+1$ eigenvector and decays along $\lambda=-1$. RK4 of the same system (blue dots) lands right on it — these eigen-modes are the normal modes.
